| 133238 | hyqd7bwMr9Kv-C5PW4n7uF4TiMnMp_hyvyhYYkYlcU8 | Active |

**Integration steps**


**Step 1 — Get authorization.**


 Obtain an OAuth2 bearer token with your
API credentials and send it as `Authorization: Bearer {access_token}`
on every call. Obtain a fresh token before it expires — an expired
token is rejected before the signature is even checked.

**Step 2 — Sign the payload.**

 Build the canonical string
`tillNo|timestamp|nonce` (pipe-joined, no whitespace) and compute
the lowercase-hex HMAC-SHA256 digest of it, keyed with your signing
secret. Generate `timestamp` and `nonce` fresh for every request,
including retries.

    import hmac, hashlib, uuid
    from datetime import datetime, timezone

    # Your credentials
    signing_secret = "<your_signing_secret_key>"
    till_value = "<your_tillNo_value>"

    # Generate fresh values for each request
    timestamp = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
    nonce = str(uuid.uuid4()).lower()

    # Build and sign
    signing_string = f"{till_value}|{timestamp}|{nonce}"
    signature = hmac.new(
        signing_secret.encode("utf-8"),
        signing_string.encode("utf-8"),
        hashlib.sha256
    ).hexdigest()

    # Add to requestParameters:
    # "timestamp": timestamp, "nonce": nonce, "signature": signature

Sandbox till number and signing secret are issued to you on the
Developer Portal — use those values in place of the placeholders
above, and never commit a secret key to source control or ship it
in client-side code. Your production secret and till number are
available on the Merchant Portal once you go live.

**Step 3 — Build the request body.**

 Assemble the service envelope
(`serviceCode`, `txnReference`, `requestParameters`) with the signed
`timestamp`, `nonce` and `signature` nested inside
`requestParameters` alongside `tillNo`, `payMblNo`, `amount`,
`extRefNo` and `callBackUrl`. See ProcessNeoMerchantStkRequest
below.

    {
      "serviceCode": "NEO_MRCHNT_STK",
      "txnReference": "016e8669-f7e2-442d-b37b-7df8d4e0f8a7",
      "requestParameters": {
        "tillNo": "127041",
        "payMblNo": "0704540384",
        "amount": "2",
        "extRefNo": "12312312",
        "callBackUrl": "https://your-domain.com/webhook",
        "timestamp": "2026-08-07T10:30:00Z",
        "nonce": "7f768f08-20e5-4720-ba6c-5431f67e3c5c",
        "signature": "a3f8b2c1d0e9..."
      }
    }

**Step 4 — Send the request**

 POST the signed body with your bearer
token to `/services/process-request`. The call is
synchronous and confirms only that the request was accepted for
processing — not that the customer has approved the prompt.

**Step 5 — Read the response.**

 HTTP 200 confirms the gateway accepted
the request. Check `data.serviceTransactionStatus` for the
processing outcome (COMPLETED, PENDING or FAILED), and see the
statusCode table on the 200 response below for handled-failure
codes.

**Step 6 — Handle the completion callback.**

 Once the customer responds
to the prompt, LOOP POSTs the outcome to the `callBackUrl` supplied
in Step 3. Acknowledge it with a 2xx quickly, stay idempotent on
`txnReference`, and only release goods on this callback — never on
the Step 5 response alone. See CompletionCallbackPayload; per the
developer guide, the exact callback field set is still to be
confirmed by the LOOP integrations team, so treat any fields beyond
`statusCode` and `txnReference` as provisional until confirmed for
your integration.

**Step 7 — Handle failures and retries.**

 On a 503 statusCode (prompt
could not be delivered), retry after a short delay, and confirm the
customer's mobile number is correct and active if it persists. On
any 400/401 statusCode, correct the payload or your credentials
before retrying — resending it unchanged fails the same way. See
the statusCode table on the 200 response below for the full set of
causes and resolutions.

**Step 8 — Test in sandbox, then go live.**

 Sandbox till number and
signing secret are issued on the Developer Portal for testing; do
not use them in production. Production credentials (secret key and
till number) are available on the Merchant Portal once your
integration is approved — everything else about the contract stays
the same.

response.name:
The gateway returns HTTP 200 for essentially every outcome, success or handled failure — branch on the `statusCode` field inside the response body, not the HTTP status line:

| statusCode | Cause | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | Success | The request was accepted; check `data.serviceTransactionStatus` for the processing outcome. |
| 400 | Timestamp is expired or set in the future. | Generate a fresh UTC timestamp at the time of the request. |
| 400 | Nonce has already been used. | Generate a new unique nonce for every request — never reuse one, even on retry. |
| 400 | Signing fields are at the request root instead of inside requestParameters. | Move timestamp, nonce and signature into the requestParameters object. |
| 400 | A required field is missing or has an invalid value. | Review all required parameters and ensure values match the expected format. |
| 401 | Bearer token is missing, invalid, or expired. | Generate a fresh token from the authorization endpoint and retry. |
| 401 | Signature verification failed. | Check the signing string order (tillNo, then timestamp, then nonce), confirm the correct secret key is used, and verify hex encoding. |
| 503 | The payment prompt could not be delivered to the customer's device. | Retry after a short delay. If the issue persists, verify the customer's mobile number is correct and active. |

data is an empty object `{}` on every non-200 statusCode.

description.content: Added as a part of security scheme: oauth2

Mpesa Prompt (LOOP STK Push) — send a payment request to your
customer's phone. Your customer receives a prompt on their device,
reviews the amount, and taps to approve. The payment is collected into
your merchant till once approved; if the customer does not respond or
declines, no payment is made. The call is synchronous (it returns once
the request has been accepted), but the actual outcome is confirmed
asynchronously on the callBackUrl supplied with the request. See the
Integration steps in the operation description below.
